questions.q: Find a word in paragraph 3 meaning 'state of mind / how you feel': people's ___ tends to suffer.

task: ¿Cómo usas tú las redes sociales: de forma activa o pasiva? Escribe 80–100 palabras y propone un hábito para mejorar.
paragraphs: We have never been so connected. Most of us carry a phone that lets us talk to friends on the other side of the world in seconds. And yet many surveys suggest that more people, especially young adults, say they often feel lonely. Is social media part of the problem?

The answer seems to depend on how we use it. Researchers often make a distinction between "active" and "passive" use. Active use means messaging friends, commenting, or organising to meet in person. Passive use means scrolling through other people's posts without interacting. Several studies have found that passive scrolling is more likely to make people feel worse, partly because we compare our ordinary lives with the carefully chosen highlights of other people's.

Time also matters. When hours online replace sleep, exercise or face-to-face conversations, people's mood tends to suffer. On the other hand, for people who are isolated, for example because of illness, disability or living far from family, online communities can be a real lifeline.

So what can we do? Experts suggest some simple habits: turn off notifications that are not important, avoid using your phone during meals, and use social media to arrange real meetings rather than to replace them. Some people also try a "digital detox", spending a day or a weekend completely offline.
Technology itself is neither good nor bad. As one psychologist put it, "Social media is like a kitchen knife. It depends on what you do with it."
